mission.primary: low-speed trail carving with snowboard-like progressive handling

hard_requirements.fail_safe_control_bias: any traction/carve assist must fall back to symmetric bounded torque

ride_targets.rider_interface: independent left/right fit with easy emergency step-off

charging.dock_goal: protected alignment dock or stand with no exposed traction contacts
charging.pack_swap: power-off/cold-swap only until a qualified battery system explicitly supports otherwise
charging.compatibility_rule: use only a charger explicitly approved for the selected battery/system

mission_energy_strategy.installed_energy_policy: select the smallest qualified pack class that covers the mission with reserve
mission_energy_strategy.trip_energy_policy: do not equate maximum available trip energy with permanently installed energy
mission_energy_strategy.trail_class_role: default handling/carryability reference when mission range permits
mission_energy_strategy.range_class_role: long-mission reference when added mass is justified
mission_energy_strategy.cold_swap_role: powered-off logistics option only; not a reason to body-carry an unprotected traction pack
mission_energy_strategy.telemetry_upgrade: replace planning Wh/mi with qualified X1 telemetry when powered commissioning eventually exists

charge_dock.electrical_rule: preserve the selected battery/system-approved charger and connector interface

required_signals: at least one non-driven wheel speed or equivalent independent ground-speed reference

modes.powder: soft jerk, progressive carve response, conservative slip limiting
modes.trail: responsive low-speed torque with bounded slip
modes.range: soft acceleration and efficiency-biased power limits
modes.shasta: very-low jerk, low speed cap, predictable symmetric torque and braking

carve_assist.method: small bounded left/right drive torque bias

hard_boundaries: remote deadman required
board-mounted leash attachment prohibited
deliberate differential carve assist disabled
independent mechanical brake remains required
no dog in software, bench, or initial rider-only powered qualification
dog introduction requires future explicit companion authority
current slew is not physical jerk authority

whether 200x50 tire compliance is sufficient after rider-specific pressure tuning
whether PowerLam deck ride feel is preferable to snowboard-composite alternatives for this rider

strengths: narrowest published deck envelope among the three Rev-C stance candidates
brake-compatible Matrix III and Rockstar II architecture
only 1.3lb heavier complete than the Comp 95 reference
F5X snowboard-style binding angle adjustment is directly supported
open_questions: whether stiff high-pop construction is too reactive or fatiguing for low-speed trail carving
whether current waitlist availability makes it practical as the first donor
exact received product/SKU revision because the current page title and embedded specs expose 10407 versus 10406

whether 284mm deck is unnecessarily wide for rider leverage

received-board mass and exact electric truck configuration

strengths: same nominal diameter class as 8-inch architecture
open_questions: V5 brake is not currently listed by MBS as directly compatible with Rockstar Pro II XL
whether extra width materially improves this rider's loose-surface control

lessons: large pneumatic air volume can improve bump absorption and traction
low ride height matters even with a larger tire
ride shaping is a product-level feature, not just throttle scaling
independent suspension can dramatically increase rough-terrain isolation
suspension and large battery capacity impose a substantial mass penalty
sealed gear drive is a useful durability benchmark
a complete vendor-engineered front hydraulic brake architecture exists for mountainboards
front braking can preserve rear axle volume for a conventional rear 2WD drivetrain
the lesson is the integrated truck/hub/disc/brake system, not permission to adapt Magura hardware onto Matrix trucks

known.brake: Magura HS11 hydraulic rim-brake actuator adapted by TRAMPA to custom wheel discs

lessons: current integrated high-voltage battery references consume a large fraction of the desired total vehicle mass
trail and range mass goals must be treated as aspirational until drive, ESC, guard, enclosure and mounting masses are budgeted
quick-swap smaller packs remain attractive when a large installed pack harms handling or carryability

risks: front-drive traction decreases under uphill acceleration
front electric truck width may differ from rear brake truck

risks: V5 rotor/arm/cable and drive occupy overlapping wheel-end packaging
vendor compatibility statements do not prove simultaneous coexistence
